summary_md:
**Arky Yang ([@arkyyang](https://x.com/arkyyang/status/2115076613461418010))** gives a builder-oriented digest of the arXiv preprint **"Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses,"** which compares 17 ways a harness can make a coding agent check its own work.

- **Agents seldom self-check:** only a small share (~6–14%) of edit turns were followed by a test/check before the next edit, and simply telling the agent to verify helped little.
- **An independent critic wins:** a fresh-context reviewer model added roughly 6–9.5 points on Terminal-Bench and 4–6.6 on SWE-bench at modest extra cost, whereas "reject the first *done*" completion gates helped but cost ~1.6–1.8×.
- **Review the diff, not the transcript:** critics that saw only code changes beat those that saw the whole trajectory, and were cheaper.
- **More review has diminishing returns:** extra rounds or critics added up to ~3.5 more points.

Arky also summarizes the setup: four layers of verification design, several open coding models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, MiniMax) with a Qwen critic, plus a new expert-judged VisualBench.
relevance: Evidence-backed design guidance for harness builders: add a diff-only critic step before investing in retry loops or prompt nagging.
